question: Should OpenClaw adopt this shared localization package and optional Gateway command-localization contract as the supported cross-core and plugin presentation boundary?
rationale: The branch changes product architecture and protocol-adjacent metadata across channels, Gateway, UI, skills, and plugins; tests and a partial recording cannot choose the permanent ownership and compatibility policy.

options.title: Sponsor a staged contract rollout
options.body: Confirm the shared presentation contract and land it in reviewable slices with compatibility coverage and exact-head proof for the surfaces each slice changes.

options.title: Limit the initial scope
options.body: Keep localization inside existing surface-owned catalogs and defer Gateway/plugin metadata extensions until an owner-approved public contract is designed.

options.title: Pause the RFC series
options.body: Leave the draft open but do not merge the shared contract until maintainers select a localization architecture and rollout policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged contract rollout
recommendation.body: Confirm the shared presentation contract and land it in reviewable slices with compatibility coverage and exact-head proof for the surfaces each slice changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor is the visible RFC and series proposer, making them the best available routing contact for clarifying the proposed contract; a current-main area owner was not established from the available review evidence.
